claims.text: Local atomic-level chemical heterogeneity governs the premelting behavior of HEA nanoparticles.
Local atomic-level chemical heterogeneity governs the melting behavior of HEA nanoparticles.
Chemical heterogeneity influences the distribution of cohesive energy across nanoparticle surfaces and cores.
Changing the number and type of constituent elements systematically changes chemical heterogeneity or elemental mixing entropy.
The relevant structural mediator is the distribution of cohesive energy across the nanoparticle, especially the difference between surface and core cohesive energies.
Increased chemical heterogeneity produces a broader distribution of cohesive energies.
A broader distribution of cohesive energies lowers the energy barrier for surface-atom diffusion.
Lowering the barrier for surface-atom diffusion destabilizes the nanoparticle surface at lower temperatures.
Lower-temperature surface destabilization influences the onset of premelting and melting.
Nanoparticles with higher chemical heterogeneity or mixing entropy will have a lower premelting onset temperature than nanoparticles with lower heterogeneity.
Nanoparticles with higher chemical heterogeneity or mixing entropy will have a broader premelting temperature range than nanoparticles with lower heterogeneity.
The predicted lower premelting onset and broader premelting range apply relative to single-element nanoparticles of comparable size and morphology.
The hypothesis is expected to hold for HEA nanoparticles from 1 to 100 nm in size.
The hypothesis is expected to hold for compositions containing at least three constituent elements when mixing entropy is significant.
Nanoparticle size and surface energy may also affect premelting behavior.
DSC and in-situ TEM can be used to measure premelting onset, premelting range, and melting temperature in the proposed nanoparticle series.

contradictions.description: The stated domain requires at least three constituent elements, but the proposed test series includes binary alloys and describes the entire series as HEA nanoparticles. Binary samples fall outside the hypothesis's stated compositional range.
